A silk tie that knows how to pull a look together without acting like the loudest man in the room. Done in forest with navy, brown and cream stripes, it is a smooth operator for weddings, work, and anywhere you want to look like you have got excellent taste and at least one decent plan.
Q: How do I wear a silk tie without looking like I’m off to corporate court?
A: Silk ties get a bad rap as the strict uniform of middle management, but a 100% woven silk tie is actually one of the easiest ways to inject texture and personality into modern tailoring. It’s all about opting for rich weaves (like jacquard, birdseye, or grenadine) over flat, shiny synthetics.
Here is how to style it, Percival style:
Subvert the Suit: Knot your silk tie under an unbuttoned Cuban collar shirt, layered beneath a unstructured suit jacket. Pair with wide-leg trousers and loafers to strike the perfect balance between sharp and nonchalant.
The High-Low Mix: Skip the full suit entirely. Wear a silk knit or textured jacquard tie under a buttoned Oxford shirt, layered underneath a heavy cotton twill chore jacket or fireman clasp coat for an effortless East London workwear look.

p-ironheart-10535856865546.d:
To a great extent, our ultra heavy flannel (UHF) shirts define Iron Heart: heavy, rugged, but amazingly wearable. The 12oz fabric is woven with Aspero cotton from the foothills of the Andes mountains. We double brush it on the inside and single brush it on the outside, resulting in a very soft yet substantial, thick, warm and windproof flannel. This shirt is a wardrobe staple, shown here in our western cut with a grey plaid that features a playful pop of yellow, and finished with black snaps.
Because we now use a reactive dyeing process for our UHF fabrics — as opposed to the direct dye technique used on older variations — this plaid features a subtler colour palette compared to the vibrant checks from previous seasons. Whereas those older direct-dyed fabrics would mellow in appearance after a few washes, this newer dyeing method is far more colourfast. To counter this, we’ve muted the colours slightly to offer a more worn-in appearance from the get-go.

The first product from Wythe. These oxfords were inspired by vintage American oxfords from the 1960's worn by every leading man from Miles Davis to Paul Newman.
We kept the original generous button down collar that is unlined for an expressive roll that looks just as great button or left unbuttoned and left to fly. p-ironheart-10445007683850.d:
The Barbican — subtle curves meet architectural precision to create a versatile classic. This special edition is hand-customised for us in BOLD's East London workshop, featuring a BOLD x Iron Heart engraving on the inner right arm.
BOLD London is a boutique eyewear brand born from a passion for crafting exquisite, impeccably constructed frames using the finest materials and time-honoured British artisanal techniques. Each pair is meticulously sculpted by hand from premium cellulose acetate. First, the raw shape is cut from a block, then filed into shape before heat is applied to manipulate the curvature. The frames are then buffed and polished by hand before undergoing an intensive tumbling process—for up to 48 hours—to achieve a flawlessly smooth, even finish.
Built for durability and distinction, one of BOLD’s signature design elements is the extra thickness in the front and sides of the frame, enhancing strength while remaining lightweight. This model is constructed using robust 7-barrel rivet hinges and fitted with Carl Zeiss mid grey subtle gradient lenses, offering style and superior optical performance.
